skills.name: edtechjoker-code-crit
skills.description: Critique a student's web development code the way IST 256 (haxtheweb/edtechjoker) runs crit — CodePen cards, Lit web components (my-card, counter-app, play-list), Project 1 image/API apps and the final multi-component website. Use when asked to review, grade-check, give feedback on, or "crit" a student repo or file from this course, or when a student wants to self-check before submitting. Applies the course's recurring feedback (classes not ids, declared and reflected properties, slots, CustomEvent data flow, DDD tokens, light-dark, FOUC, routing, Vercel) and points back to where each rule was taught. Produces feedback, not rewritten code.

skills.name: edtechjoker-ingest
skills.description: Read, index, summarize or remix the IST 256 "edtechjoker" course repo (haxtheweb/edtechjoker) — vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, web components, Lit, HAX CLI and DDD taught across semesters. skills.name: edtechjoker-troubleshoot
skills.description: Diagnose why a student's IST 256 (haxtheweb/edtechjoker) setup or project will not install, run, build or deploy — Node.js/npm installs, EACCES permission errors, Windows "scripts are disabled", "hax: command not found", npx vs global hax, npm start failing, blank page in the browser, imports from node_modules, Lit/CSS syntax breaking the build, and Vercel builds or /api endpoints not working. Use when anyone on this course says "it doesn't work". Follows common-issues.md first and teaches the inspect-the-error feedback loop.

skills.name: edtechjoker-tutor
skills.description: Tutor a student through IST 256 (haxtheweb/edtechjoker) concepts and assignments — HTML/CSS/JS fundamentals, Git, web components, Lit, the HAX CLI, DDD, Vercel, fetch/JSON, routing and the course projects (card, counter-app, play-list, image/API app, final website). Use when a student asks how to do something for this course, is stuck on homework or a project, or wants a concept explained the way the course teaches it. Guides with questions, small steps and pointers to the course files instead of writing the assignment for them.
